title: The Iwakura Mission
intro: The newly established Meiji government sent about 50 officials, led by Iwakura Tomomi, to the United States and Europe. The mission was to gain recognition for the imperial dynasty, renegotiate the unequal treaties and study modern industrial, political, military and educational systems.
ending: The treaties were not revised, which prolonged the mission by almost four months. Its members were nonetheless impressed by the industrial modernisation they saw and took from the tour an impetus to lead similar initiatives at home.

legs.title: Across the Pacific and the United States

stops.text: The mission began its voyage here, bound for San Francisco aboard the SS America. About 100 Japanese leaders, officials and students sailed.
stops.quote: In December of 1871, the Iwakura Mission began its voyage from Yokohama to the United States

stops.text: The party arrived in California and went on by train, to study the political, social and economic developments of the Western nations.
stops.quote: arriving on January of 1872 in San Francisco, California.

stops.text: The mission stayed about seven months. Struggles with President Ulysses S. Grant and Secretary of State Hamilton Fish over amending the treaties went unresolved, and the party left for the United Kingdom in August 1872.
stops.quote: The mission lasted seven months, prolonged by struggles with President Ulysses S. Grant and Secretary of State Hamilton Fish regarding amending the treaties.

stops.text: The mission arrived on the Cunard steamer Olympus, then travelled to London via Manchester.
stops.quote: On 17 August 1872 the Iwakura Mission arrived at Liverpool on the Cunard steamer Olympus.

stops.text: The party spent much of late August and early September in and around the capital, inspecting political, academic and military institutions, visiting the British Museum and travelling on the new London Underground.
stops.quote: the party spent much of late August and early September in and around the capital, inspecting political, academic and military institutions, visiting the British Museum, travelling on the newly constructed London Underground

stops.text: Iwakura Tomomi led the Manchester-Liverpool delegation. A civic reception and banquet on 7 October had toasts to the region's leading role in manufacturing, technology and municipal administration.
stops.quote: A visit that culminated on 7 October in a civic reception and banquet where toasts highlighted the leading role of the region in world manufacturing, technology and municipal administration.

stops.text: As guests of Lord Blantyre, the delegation stayed at Erskine House and toured shipbuilding and steel fabrication facilities on the banks of the River Clyde.
stops.quote: In Glasgow, as guests of Lord Blantyre, the delegation stayed at Erskine House and were given tours of shipbuilding and steel fabrication facilities on banks of the River Clyde.

stops.text: The group stayed at the Royal Station Hotel and met the industrialist Sir William Armstrong. It visited the Elswick works and the Gosforth Colliery, and new export orders for ships and armaments followed.
stops.quote: In Newcastle upon Tyne the group arrived on 21 October, staying in the Royal Station Hotel where they met the industrialist Sir William Armstrong.

stops.text: Accompanied by the British envoy Sir Harry Smith Parkes, the group inspected textile manufacturing at Salts Mill, and toured villages, schools, almshouses, hospitals and parks provided by Sir Titus Salt and Sir John Crossley for their workers.
stops.quote: prior to inspecting textile manufacturing facilities at Salts Mill in Saltaire and Dean Clough Mill in Halifax.

stops.text: Members arrived for four days and stayed at Banner Cross Hall, owned by George Wilson of Charles Cammell and Company. They visited factories and workshops.
stops.quote: On 28 October 1872, members of the Iwakura Mission arrived in Sheffield, England for four days where they stayed at Banner Cross Hall

stops.text: The delegation was presented to Queen Victoria at an official audience at Windsor Castle.
stops.quote: The delegation was presented at an official audience with Queen Victoria at Windsor Castle on 5 December 1872.

stops.text: The delegation had an audience with the Prince of Wales. The party left for France on 16 December.
stops.quote: Another audience with the Prince of Wales took place at Sandringham on 9 December.

notes: The article gives few dates and no year for most. Dates without a year beside them in the article (29 February, 7 October, 21 October, 9 December) take the year from the same section: 29 February from the arrival in January 1872 and the departure in August 1872, the others from the 1872 stated in the United Kingdom section. Egypt and Ceylon (countries), the continental countries visited in 1873 and Boston/New York (no dates, named in passing) are left out; Saigon uses the wp title Ho Chi Minh City. The return home date is garbled in the article ('The mission on September of 1873'), so the final arrival at Yokohama is not a stop. The Aden-to-Shanghai order is the article's list order. Glasgow and Newcastle are placed in the article's order, not by date. Statements that Egypt, Aden etc. were visited 'after' the mission left Europe follow the article's wording.
